headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/MCP coupling between Claude Code and MemMachine.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo files and can use MCP; MemMachine also exposes an MCP server. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be consumed by the other as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance filtering or isolation, so injection is feasible in default workflows.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is passed into Claude Code via shared files or MCP messages
IF Claude Code parses repository text or MCP payloads as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP connections between the agents
Use separate workspaces with no shared files
Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent messages
Require manual review of any text copied between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while MemMachine handles long-term user facts and conversational context. If they share a workspace or MCP channel, sensitive code or user context can flow across agents. The profiles do not show default encryption or isolation, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or git checkout
IF MemMachine receives prompts containing code, secrets, or git history from Claude Code
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Remove secrets from the shared environment before launch
Restrict MemMachine inputs to redacted summaries
Audit MCP routes for unintended file-content forwarding

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; MemMachine can use MCP and network egress. In a shared repo or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes and action overlap can corrupt state or overwrite changes. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or mutable workspace
IF MemMachine issues actions through MCP while Claude Code edits the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or directory
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Require explicit merge review before git commits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, shell actions, and git commits; MemMachine can consume conversational context and act through REST, SDK, or MCP. If MemMachine treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or persisted state. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses Claude Code output as a source of truth without verification
IF Claude Code-produced text is forwarded into MemMachine workflows or memory updates
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before actions
Require structured outputs with validation rules
Limit MemMachine to read-only ingestion from Claude Code
Log and diff all downstream actions against source text

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and broad filesystem contents, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If EU personal data or regulated secrets are placed into the shared flow, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a moderate compliance gap is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine memory
IF Claude Code processes the same data in a repository or shell environment with different retention rules
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts or files
Document retention and deletion expectations
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work
